Servile

/SUR-vyle/ - the stress falls on SUR · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Servile means excessively submissive and eager to please.

The valet's servile murmur of agreement followed the baron from room to room like a draft.

Worked Example

The commis chef tastes nothing until the head chef tastes first. He asks permission to salt the water, thanks the head chef twice for every correction, and last week called his own knife work clumsy because the head chef frowned at an onion. The kitchen has stopped expecting him to have opinions.

Servile is the exact word for the commis, because servile means excessively submissive and eager to please — the excess is what the word faults. Respectful keeps its footing: a respectful junior speaks politely and still says what she thinks; the servile one has handed his opinions over with his coat.

How Strong Is It? — respectful → servile → groveling

respectful vs. servile

respectful vs. servile: Respectful keeps its footing — a respectful junior lawyer lets the partner speak first and still argues her own view.

groveling vs. servile

groveling vs. servile: Groveling goes further than servile — the servile aide flatters and agrees, while the groveler throws dignity away outright, begging where he could simply ask.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — serv

Root — serv: slave (Latin servus)

Suffix — -ile

Suffix — -ile: of the nature of

Put it together

Put it together: Serv (slave — Latin servus) + -ile (of the nature of) = slave-natured. Latin servilis described what belonged to enslaved people as a class, and the English word keeps the sting: servile conduct is free behavior sliding into slavishness, submission past anything the situation demands.

Use the root in a new word: servitude

Use the root in a new word: servitude: Servitude is the condition the root names — years of forced service; the word survives in old legal sentences, 'ten years' penal servitude.'

Word Choice

critical / disdainful

Servile is an accusation: submission has gone past courtesy into self-erasure. Its unit-mates grade the slope — obedience does what it is told and keeps its dignity, docile is simply easy to lead, compliant just meets the rules. Call conduct servile when the eagerness to please has started costing someone their standing.
